Jacy Dyer.b:
Former Rocket and Varsity T Hall of Famer Jacy Dyer was named the head women's swimming & diving coach at the University of Toledo in April of 2024.
Dyer is one of the most decorated swimmers in Toledo history and returned to the Glass City after serving at James Madison, Virginia Tech, as the head coach for the men's and women's programs at Fairfield University, and also served as the head coach for the women's swimmers at the 2023 University World Games in Chengdu, China.
Dyer was named Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) Coach of the Year after guiding the Fairfield women to the 2023 MAAC Championships title in her first year at the helm. Additionally, Dyer helped mentor Erini Pappas, who was named MAAC Women's Most Outstanding Swimmer of the Meet at the 2023 MAAC Championships.
Fairfield had another successful season under Dyer's direction this past year as well, with the women finishing runner-up and the men placing fourth at the 2024 MAAC Championship meet. The Stags also collected numerous awards including MAAC Women's Most Outstanding Swimmer, men's and women's MAAC Most Outstanding Diver, and men's and women's MAAC Diving Rookie of the Year. Dyer was named MAAC Women's Swimming Coach of the Year for a second time.
Before her time at Fairfield, Dyer served as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator from 2018-22 at Virginia Tech before being promoted to associate head coach for the Hokies during the 2021-22 season. Both the men's and women's teams reached the 2022 NCAA Championships, where the women finished 23rd, the third-highest finish in program history, and the men tied for a program-best 11thplace finish. Dyer coached multiple swimmers who went on to qualify for the U.S. Junior World Championships, the World University Games, as well as the Olympics.
Before making the move to Virginia Tech, Dyer was the assistant women's swimming coach at James Madison University from 2014-18, helping the Dukes to a Colonial Athletic Association (CAA) Championship win in 2018 and three consecutive runner-up finishes. Dyer coached the squad to 31 podium finishes at the CAA Championships, nine NCAA B Cut times, six school records, and four pool records.
A native of Lebanon, Pa., Dyer graduated with a degree in psychology from the University of Toledo in 2011. She immediately started her coaching career with the Rockets and served as an assistant coach for three seasons. With Dyer on staff, Toledo captured its second MAC Championship title in 2012.
Dyer was a four-time All-MAC honoree, 2010 MAC Swimmer of the Year and UT Female Athlete of the Year, a 10-time MAC Champion with six other top-three finishes at the conference meet, and the only Rocket to ever qualify for the NCAA Championships in three separate events in her career from 2007-11. Dyer was also a 2012 Olympic Trials qualifier in the 400 and 800 freestyle and earned a world ranking of 38th in the 1650 freestyle. She was inducted into the University of Toledo Varsity T Hall of Fame in 2017.
Dyer made an immediate impact for the Rockets, breaking three school records as a freshman in the 500, 1,000, and 1,650 freestyle events. During her sophomore campaign, Dyer set the MAC record in the 500 freestyle at the conference meet. As a junior in 2010, Dyer collected five MAC individual titles, was named MAC Swimmer of the Year, and helped Toledo to its first-ever MAC Championship crown. At that meet, Dyer broke her record in the 500 freestyle (4:44.23) which still stands as the program record. As a senior, Dyer won four more MAC titles and qualified and competed at the NCAA Championships in the 200 freestyle, 500 freestyle, and mile.
WHAT THEY'RE SAYING ABOUT JACY
“Jacy is a phenomenal coach and person. She is knowledgeable, passionate, and personable. She will be an excellent head coach at Toledo, and I have no doubt she will create a positive, competitive culture and lead the team to success on every level. Such a great hire and I cannot wait to see what she accomplishes there. I am so excited for Jacy and Toledo.” - Dane Pederson, JMU Head Swimming & Diving Coach
"What I learned about Jacy is that she is a phenomenal coach, and probably an even better person. She's in it for the right reasons. She cares about people and she has a positivity that works well from a coaching standpoint, that works well for being a great teammate in this department and also works well on the recruiting trail.” - Bryan B. Blair, the University of Toledo Vice President/ Director of Athletics.

Will Jansen.b:
Will Jansen joined the University of Toledo women's swimming & diving team as the diving coach in August of 2026.
Jansen comes to the Rockets after a collegiate diving career at Indiana (2022-25), where he competed in Big Ten Championships. Following his time with the Hoosiers, Jansen served as the head coach at the Johansen Diving Academy where he coached young diving athletes.
"I am honored to join the University of Toledo swimming & diving team as the diving coach," said Jansen. "I look forward to empowering our student-athletes both in the pool and as individuals. My goal is to ensure that every athlete in this program leaves the pool trusting themselves and their abilities."
A native of Fishers, Ind., Jansen earned his bachelor's degree in exercise science from Indiana.

Mia Cheatwood.b:
Mia Cheatwood was named the assistant women's swimming & diving coach in May of 2026.
Cheatwood joins the Rockets after a four-year swimming career at West Virginia (2022-24) and Louisville (2024-26). Throughout her time as a student-athlete, Cheatwood competed in three NCAA Swimming & Diving Championships and earned All-American honors with the Cardinals in 2025 and 2026. She also scored in the 200 breaststroke in the 2026 NCAA Championships, ranking 10th in the nation.
Cheatwood ranks second in Louisville history in the 200 breaststroke (2:06.40) and third in the 100 breaststroke (58.59). As a Mountaineer, she broke the program records for both the 100 breaststroke (59.73) and 200 breaststroke (2:09.13).
Cheatwood participated in the USA Olympic Trials and was a World Trials qualifier in 2024 and 2025. She is also involved in USA Swimming, both as a participant and a coach.
A native of Bowling Green, Ohio, Cheatwood earned her bachelor's degree in public health from Louisville.
